topic.name: Expressing an Arithmetic Series in Sigma Notation

question.text: An arithmetic series has $a_3=-16$ and $a_8=-51,$ where $a_3$ and $a_8$ are the third and eighth terms of the series, respectively. What is the sum of the first $10$ terms of the series, expressed using sigma notation?
question.explanation:
Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference:

\begin{align} d &= \dfrac{a_8-a_3}{8-3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-51 - (-16)}{5} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-35}{5} \\[5pt] &= -7 \end{align}

As $a_{3}=-16$, using the formula for the $n$th term, we can compute $a_1$, as follows:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] -16 &= a_1 + (3-1)(-7) \\[3pt] -16 &= a_1 - 14 \\[3pt] a_1 &= -2 \end{align*}

So we have $a_1 = -2$ and $d=-7.$ Thus, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= -2+ (n-1)(-7) \\[3pt] &= -2 - 7n+7 \\[3pt] & = -7n+5 \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the first ten terms can be written as:

\begin{align*} \sum_{n=1}^{10} (-7n+5) \end{align*}

example.title: Writing an Arithmetic Series Using Sigma Notation Given Two Terms of the Series

question.text:
Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

\[ -12 - 7 - 2 + 3 + 8 + \ldots + 28 + 33 \]
question.explanation:
The first term $a_1=-12$ and the common difference is:

\begin{align} d &= a_2 - a_1 \\[3pt] &=-7-(-12) \\[3pt] &=5 \end{align}

Hence, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= -12 + (n-1)(5) \\[3pt] &=-12 + 5n-5 \\[3pt] &=5n - 17 \end{align*}

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the $n$th term:

\begin{align*} a_n &= 33 \\[3pt] 5n - 17 &= 33 \\[3pt] 5n & = 33 + 17 \\[3pt] 5n & = 50 \\[3pt] n &= 10 \end{align*}

There are $10$ terms in total, from $n=1$ to $n=10.$ So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

\[ \sum_{n=1}^{10} (5n - 17) \]

example.title: Writing an Arithmetic Series Using Sigma Notation when Not All Terms are Shown

question.text:
Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

\[ 1 + \dfrac 53 + \dfrac 73+ \ldots +\dfrac{37}{3}+13 \]
question.explanation:
The first term $a_1=1$ and the common difference is:

\begin{align} d &= a_2 - a_1 \\[3pt] &=\dfrac 53- 1 \\[5pt] &=\dfrac 23 \end{align}

Hence, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= 1+ (n-1)\left( \dfrac 23 \right) \\[5pt] &=1 + \dfrac 23n - \dfrac 23 \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{3}n + \dfrac 13 \end{align*}

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the $n$th term:

\begin{align*} a_n &= 13 \\[3pt] \dfrac{2}{3}n + \dfrac 13 &= 13 \\[5pt] \dfrac 23n & =\dfrac{38}{3} \\[5pt] n &= 19 \end{align*}

There are $19$ terms in total, from $n=1$ to $n=19.$ So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

\[ \sum_{n=1}^{19} \left( \dfrac{2}{3}n + \dfrac 13 \right) \]
